sentences.text: Misc. Appeal No. 6807 of 2023

Smt. Radha Bai And Others
 Versus
 Shahrukh And Others
 Appearance:
Shri Anshul Shrivastava, learned counsel for the ap  Shri Anshul Dabhade, learned counsel for the respon  Shri Akshansh Mehra, learned counsel for the respon  ORDER
The appellants have filed this appeal being aggrieved by the award dated 18.08.2023 passed in claim case No.4/2022 challenging the quantum of compensation.
2. The short facts of the case are that on 24.12.2020, the deceased Kamal went along with Deepak to attend the marriage of brother-in-law Devesh at village-Chandkhedi.

When they were returning from Chandkhedi to Shaamgarh by motorcycle registration No.MP14-NB-7984, as soon as they reached near Donopolo Factory, dumper No.RJ17-GA-5967 came from the side of Shaamgarh which was being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and dashed into the motorcycle of Kamal because of which Kamal and Deepak sustained grievous injuries, Kamal was admitted in Community Health Center, Shaamgarh from where he was referred to 2 MA-6807-2023 District Hospital, Mandsaur.
He was further referred to Mewad Hospital Mandsaur.
He was ultimately taken to Paras J.K. Hospital, Udaipur, Rajasthan.

With effect from 24.12.2022 the deceased Kamal went in coma and his treatment continued and ultimately on 10.04.2021 he died while being treated at Maharana Bhoopal Raajkiya Chikitsaalay, Udaipur, Rajasthan.
3. The claimants/ appellants filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the death of Kamal.
The claims tribunal after assessing the evidence on record awarded total compensation of Rs.19,71,200/- out of which the amount for loss of dependency was Rs.9,07,200/-.

The amount of Rs.9,53,619/- was of medical bills and Rs.40,000/-
was for loss of consortium and after adding compensation in other heads, the aforesaid amount of Rs.19,71,200/- was awarded.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that he challenges the award on two counts: first,
income of the deceased was assessed very low and second, the compensation for loss of consortium has not been awarded to all five claimants.
For buttressing his submission, he refers to para 31 of the award and submits that there were two persons who sustained injuries in the accident i.e. Deepak and Kamal.
Kamal has died and Deepak sustained grievous injuries.

1 i.e. Deepak was considered by the claims tribunal in para 31 of the award, significantly, both deceased and Deepak claimed that they were working as barbers but, in the case of Deepak his income was considered at Rs.9000/- per month on notional basis 3 MA-6807-2023 by disbelieving his claim at Rs.15000/- per month whereas in the case of the deceased- Kamal, the income was considered as Rs.4500/- by disbelieving his claim of income of Rs.500/- per day.

sentences.text: The claims tribunal did not assign any reason for such different assessment of income though in both claims they were working as barbers.
Both were residents of villages of same vicinity.
In both cases the claims tribunal has taken notional income by disbelieving claims.
Thus, he submits that in the case of appellant also his income should be taken as Rs.9000/- per month.

5. As regards the other submission regarding compensation for loss of consortium, he placed reliance upon the judgment of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram,
AIR OnLine 2018 SC 1249.

AIR OnLine 2018 SC 1249
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. Per contra, learned counsel for the insurance company submits that in the present case, insurance company has been directed to pay and recover for breach of policy.
He points out that the assessment of income of the deceased is correct at Rs.4500/- per month for the reason that there may be difference in the size of villages of two persons.
It may be a case that village of the injured person is having bigger population, hence, the claims tribunal has taken income of the deceased at Rs.9000/- per month.
As far as the amount of consortium is concerned, learned counsel for the respondent supports the findings of the claims tribunal without any elaboration.
7. Learned counsel for the respondent No.2/owner also supports the arguments tendered by the learned counsel for insurance company regarding the income of the deceased.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

9. It is seen from perusal of paragraphs 30, 31 and 32 of the impugned award that the claims tribunal while assessing income of the injured -Deepak has taken income as Rs.9000/- per month although he also claims himself to be barber but while considering the income of the deceased in para 40, 41 and 42 of the award, same has been taken as Rs.4500/- per month although he also claims himself to be barber.
No specific reason is assigned in the award for taking different figures for fixing the income of two persons who claim similar calling.

Nevertheless this Court by taking support of guidelines issued by the State Legal Services Authority find that for the relevant period the minimum wages for the unskilled labourer was Rs.8400/- per month.
As such income of the deceased is taken as Rs.8400/- per month.
As regards the compensation for loss of consortium, it is seen that there are five claimants i.e. wife, two children, mother and father of the deceased.

Thus, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co.
Ltd. Vs. Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram, AIR OnLine 2018 SC 1 2 4 9 , all the five claimants are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each for compensation for consortium.

sentences.text: With the above modification and addition, now the compensation for loss of dependency would come to Rs.16,93,440/- and the amount of compensation for loss of consortium of all 5 claimants would come to Rs.2 Lacs and the total compensation changed to Rs.29,17,059/-.
The claims tribunal has already awarded amount of Rs.19,71,200/-.
Thus, the appellants are entitled to amount of Rs.9,45,859/- over and above the amount already 5 MA-6807-2023 awarded by the claims tribunal.
This enhanced amount shall carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of the application before the claims tribunal.
Rest of the conditions of the award shall remain intact.
11. With the aforesaid, the present appeal is allowed in part.
